# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 13 - **Additions**: +1397 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T19:50:15Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: doc accuracy — "Two guards" lists three bullets, and the third describes behavior that can't happen**

- "Two guards keep the pass sane" is followed by **three** bullets.
- The third bullet ("a trigger at/above the window clamps to `window` (fire at the window, never past it)") describes an unreachable outcome: `clamped = window` always satisfies `clamped >= defaultTrigger`, so that input returns `base` as a no-op two lines earlier — it never "fires at the window". The test correctly pins the no-op; the doc should say "a trigger at/above the default threshold (the window included) is a no-op".

Worth fixing while the file is new — this is the doc bench operators will read to size `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: document the preview-bound floor of the env cap**

`resolveRunSpillsConfig` lets an operator set any positive threshold, but the preview bounds stay at the defaults (`headChars + tailChars = 4000`), and `buildPreview` now renders a body that fits those bounds **in full**. So `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=1000` doesn't cap the model-visible output at ~1000 chars — a spilled body of 101–…

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 13 - **Additions**: +1397 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T19:50:15Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

## General PR Comments

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: doc accuracy — "Two guards" lists three bullets, and the third describes behavior that can't happen**

- "Two guards keep the pass sane" is followed by **three** bullets.
- The third bullet ("a trigger at/above the window clamps to `window` (fire at the window, never past it)") describes an unreachable outcome: `clamped = window` always satisfies `clamped >= defaultTrigger`, so that input returns `base` as a no-op two lines earlier — it never "fires at the window". The test correctly pins the no-op; the doc should say "a trigger at/above the default threshold (the window included) is a no-op".

Worth fixing while the file is new — this is the doc bench operators will read to size `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: document the preview-bound floor of the env cap**

`resolveRunSpillsConfig` lets an operator set any positive threshold, but the preview bounds stay at the defaults (`headChars + tailChars = 4000`), and `buildPreview` now renders a body that fits those bounds **in full**. So `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=1000` doesn't cap the model-visible output at ~1000 chars — a spilled body of 101–…

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 13 - **Additions**: +1397 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T19:50:15Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 13 - **Additions**: +1397 - **Deletions**: -22 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T19:50:15Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

```text
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. ```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

```dart

if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face.
```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Fixed on head `8548aa3e` — all 7 findings addressed and pinned by tests

## 🚨 BLOCKING — `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`

`withCompactionTriggerTokens` no longer throws: the keep clamp is guarded
(`lib/src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart`):

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max<int>(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

A parse-valid trigger of `1` degrades the keep to `1` — the same
"junk never breaks a boot" contract the parse already had — instead of
killing the run loop, the resume boot cap, or the resume parity budget.

Pinned in `test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart`:

- `triggerTokens: 1` → `keepRecentTokens == 1`, and the gate still fires
  just past the trigger (`shouldCompact(2, …)` true);
- every parse-valid spelling (`1`, `+1`, `" 1 "`) through
  `resolveBenchCompactionSettings` resolves without throwing.

Both tests failed with the reported `Invalid argument(s): 1` from
`bench_trigger.dart 59` before the fix and pass now.

## ⚠️ IMPORTANT — env knob vs explicit `compactionSettings` override

The PR-description contract was the intended one (config pin wins), so the
code was changed to match (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli.dart`,
`_effectiveCompactionSettings`):

```dart
final override = config.compactionSettings;
if (override != null) return override;
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(
  resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings,
  window: _effectiveContextWindow,
  env: environment,
);
```

`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` retunes the DEFAULTS for a bench run; it never
rewrites a user-pinned section — including `enabled: false` (the knob cannot
re-enable compaction the user switched off). Behavior is byte-identical to
pre-gh-1604 whenever a section is pinned.

Pinned by a new group in `test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart`
through the `@visibleForTesting` seam `effectiveCompactionSettingsForTest`:

- explicit pin + env → the pin verbatim (reserve/keep untouched);
- explicit `enabled: false` pin + env → stays disabled;
- no pin + env → the trigger applies (regression anchor);
- no pin + no env → `CompactionSettings.forWindow` defaults.

## 💡 Suggestions

1. **Spills notes + override notices** — `resolveRunSpillsConfig`
   (`lib/src/spill/spill.dart`) now carries `notes: base.notes` into the
   composed config, and `attachSpillWiring`
   (`lib/src/cli/agent_cli_spill.dart`) announces the retune
   (`[spills] threshold overridden via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD: 8192 → 2048`)

   the new `test/spill/spill_env_wiring_test.dart` (boots the real

   `test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart`.

   exactly two guards, and the window case is folded into the no-op guard

   the same no-op, never a "fire at the window" outcome).

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

```text
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-14):

```dart

if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.
